cards.text: Paul and his companions set sail from Paphos and land in Perga in Pamphylia. One of them is John, and at Perga, John leaves them. Every team has that one guy who looks at the map and says, "You know what, y'all go ahead."

cards.question: John leaves Paul and his companions at Perga. Where does he go back to?

cards.text: Paul and Barnabas travel inland to Pisidian Antioch, walk into the synagogue on the Sabbath, and sit down. Fresh off a showdown with a sorcerer, and they just take a seat like they're waiting for their number to get called at the DMV.

cards.question: After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders tell the two visitors to stay quiet.
The synagogue leaders send word to Paul and Barnabas, inviting them to speak. What do the leaders ask for?

cards.text: Paul stands up and motions with his hand. That's the move that means "Put the phones down, I've got something to say."

cards.question: Paul's first words call out two groups in the synagogue. Who are they?

answers.text: Men of Israel and Gentiles who fear God
Priests and Levites from the temple

cards.text: Paul starts WAY back. God chose their fathers, made them a great people in Egypt, and led them out of that land with an uplifted arm.

cards.question: Paul says God endured His people's conduct in the wilderness for about forty years.

cards.text: God vanquished seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to His people as an inheritance. All this took about 450 years, and Paul gets through it faster than I can explain what I did last Tuesday.

cards.question: After all this, God gave His people ___ until the time of Samuel the prophet.

cards.text: The people ask for a king, and God gives them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who rules forty years. Not the Saul who's also called Paul, friend, a DIFFERENT Saul, and after removing him, God raises up David as king.

cards.question: God testifies about David son of Jesse, the new king. What does God call him?

answers.text: A man after My own heart
A man with a mighty arm

cards.question: Paul says the Savior God promised comes from the descendants of Saul son of Kish.

cards.text: Before Jesus arrives, John preaches a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel. Not the John who left at Perga, a whole different John, because apparently that name came in a value pack.

cards.question: As John is completing his course, he says there's One coming after him. What does John say he isn't worthy to do for Him?

cards.text: Paul tells them this message of salvation has been sent to THEM. Then he says the people of Jerusalem and their rulers didn't recognize Jesus, and in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets read every Sabbath.

cards.question: They found no ground for a death sentence, yet they asked ___ to have Jesus executed.

cards.text: When they've carried out all that was written about Him, they take Him down from the tree and lay Him in a tomb. But God raised Him from the dead, and friend, THAT is the line this whole sermon has been baking toward.

cards.question: For many days after God raises Him, Jesus is seen by those who had traveled with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem.

cards.text: Paul says the good news is this: what God promised their fathers, He has fulfilled by raising up Jesus. Then he quotes a Psalm: "You will not let Your Holy One see decay."

cards.question: Paul says David served God's purpose in his own generation and then fell asleep. What happened to David's body?

answers.text: It was buried and saw decay
It was taken up to heaven
It was never buried at all

cards.question: Paul says forgiveness of sins is proclaimed through Jesus. Through Him, everyone who ___ is justified, the way the law of Moses never could.

cards.text: Paul doesn't wrap up with a little "thanks for having me," friend. He ends with a warning: watch out that what the prophets said doesn't happen to you, words aimed at scoffers about a work God is doing in their days.

cards.question: The prophets' warning says the scoffers would believe God's work if someone told them about it.

cards.text: The sermon's done, and Paul and Barnabas head for the door. But the people in that synagogue are not done with them.

cards.question: As Paul and Barnabas leave the synagogue, what do the people urge them to do?

answers.text: Write the message on a scroll

cards.text: After the synagogue is dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism follow Paul and Barnabas. Paul's got followers, and NOT the phone kind.

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas urge the people following them to continue in the ___ of God.

cards.text: On the following Sabbath, nearly the WHOLE city gathers to hear the word of the Lord. Friend, I live alone on a cookie planet, and my biggest crowd ever is me and the oven timer.

cards.question: But when the Jews see the crowds gathering for Paul, they are filled with ___.

cards.text: They blasphemously contradict what Paul is saying. You know that one person in the group chat who answers every single message with "Actually…"? That energy, but in person.

cards.question: Facing all that contradicting, Paul and Barnabas back down and give a quiet, careful answer.

cards.text: They say it was necessary to speak the word of God to them first. But since they reject it and don't consider themselves worthy of eternal life, something is about to change.

cards.question: Since the word is rejected, who do Paul and Barnabas say they will turn to now?
Paul and Barnabas say this is what the Lord commanded them. In the Lord's words, what has He made them?

cards.text: When the Gentiles hear this, they rejoice and glorify the word of the Lord. Somebody just told them the door is open, and they are NOT waiting to be asked twice.

cards.question: In Pisidian Antioch, all who were appointed for eternal life believe.
After all this, how far does the word of the Lord spread?

answers.text: No farther than the city gate

cards.text: But the Jews incite the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. Together they stir up persecution against Paul and Barnabas.

cards.question: What does the persecution in Pisidian Antioch do to Paul and Barnabas?

answers.text: Drives them out of the district
Puts them in the city jail

cards.question: In protest, Paul and Barnabas shake the ___ off their feet and go to ___.
Even after Paul and Barnabas are driven out, the disciples are filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

cards.text: Run out of town, and the joy is still there, the kind no amount of junk drawer dust could ever cover. Keep that apron on, friend, because this journey is not over yet.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 19 quotes "thanks for having me", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card gives no context for where this passage picks up. It is passage 2 of Paul's First Journey and starts in the middle of a trip, but the card never says the team was sent out on a journey. It also never says who Paul or John is. John's role as their helper (Acts 13:5) would explain who just left.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Paul and John are named the first time they appear, but the card never says who they are.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke gives John a reason for leaving: he looked at the map and backed out of the road ahead. Acts 13:13 gives no reason. The joke also laughs at John instead of with his situation.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Barnabas is named for the first time with no word on who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Fresh off a showdown with a sorcerer" states a Bible fact from Acts 13:6-11, the previous passage, with no reference. The card cites only Acts 13:14.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The DMV joke, "waiting for their number to get called," signals that the visitors are about to be called on. That rules out the "stay quiet" statement on card 4 before the baker answers it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "The Saul who's also called Paul" is a Bible fact from Acts 13:9, outside this passage, and it is stated with no reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to supply the wording of God's quoted testimony ("a man after My own heart"). No earlier card sets it up, so the baker can't reason their way to it. It is guessing the words of a line.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: John the Baptist is introduced only as "a whole different John." The card never says simply who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to finish John's quoted line ("whose sandals I am not worthy to untie"). Untie, carry and hold can't be reasoned out from earlier cards, so this is guessing wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question opens with "They found no ground" but never says who "they" are: the people of Jerusalem and their rulers. Card 12, which says so, is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card cites Acts 13:36-37, but the right answer (David's body was buried and saw decay) is only in Acts 13:36. Acts 13:37 is about Jesus. The citation should be Acts 13:36.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The sermon's key contrast in Acts 13:37 is never told: the One God raised did not see decay. No card carries it, so the baker meets David's decay without the payoff.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "The way the law of Moses never could" stretches Acts 13:39. The verse says believers are justified "from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses." It does not say the law never could justify.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The choice-card types in this stop mostly cycle in a fixed order: MC, TF, FB, MC, TF, MC, FB, TF, MC, FB, TF.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Leave the city before nightfall" is close to something that does happen later in the passage. Paul and Barnabas are driven out of the district (Acts 13:50).

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "They say it was necessary to speak the word of God to them first" uses "they" for both Paul and Barnabas and the Jews. It reads as if the Jews are speaking. The card also has none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: "Together they stir up persecution" says the women and leading men joined in stirring it up. Acts 13:50 just says "They stirred up persecution" and leaves open who.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "sand" is close in meaning to "dust." A baker could argue that shaking sand off their feet means the same thing.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "Run out of town, and the joy is still there" ties the disciples' joy to being driven out. Card 18's "Even after" does the same. Acts 13:52 only says "And the disciples were filled with joy" and leaves open both how the two connect and which disciples are meant.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
